result.summary: Cap timeout values in `Sock::WaitMany` to `INT_MAX` milliseconds and introduce a dedicated `Sock::NO_TIMEOUT` sentinel. `bitcoin-cli` uses this sentinel when `-rpcclienttimeout=0` is specified instead of converting the request into an arbitrary 5-year timeout.
result.problem: On platforms without `USE_POLL` such as macOS, `Sock::WaitMany` uses `select()`, which rejects timeouts greater than 10^8 seconds with `EINVAL`. Because `bitcoin-cli` previously approximated zero timeout as a 5-year duration (~1.58 * 10^8 seconds), running `bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0` on macOS immediately fails with 'Could not connect to the server'.
evidence: PR description: '`bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0` is documented as "no timeout", but on macOS it fails with "Could not connect to the server" since #34342 (it's in v32.0rc1/rc2).'
PR description: 'The new `sock_tests/wait_large_timeout` test waits with a 5 year timeout on a socket that already has data. It fails on master on macOS and passes with this change.'
result.card: bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 is documented as disabling timeouts, but it currently fails immediately on macOS with 'Could not connect to the server'. This regression occurred in #34342 because the CLI converted zero into a 5-year timeout, exceeding macOS select() limit of 10^8 seconds and returning EINVAL. This PR caps timeouts in Sock::WaitMany to INT_MAX milliseconds and adds an explicit Sock::NO_TIMEOUT mode passed as null to select() and -1 to poll().

risk.why: A flaw in socket timeout arithmetic or polling could cause network waits in bitcoin-cli or other Sock users to time out early or hang indefinitely.
